transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Doc. Thank you for fitting me in. I, uh... I hope I'm not wasting your time here. I just... well, I've been having a bit of a rough patch, I guess you could say. 

Nothing too crazy, I really don't want to make a big deal out of it, but... I've been having these thoughts lately. Just silly things, really, like... maybe my family would just be better off if I didn't wake up in the morning. It's really embarrassing to even say out loud, to be honest with you. I wouldn't normally make a fuss, but it kind of rattled me, and I ended up blurting it out to my supervisor at work. He's the one who thought I should come see someone. 

Is that... I mean, is it okay that I came in for that? I just want to make sure I'm in the right place.
Can you tell me how long you've been feeling this way—when did these low feelings and thoughts first start?

Well, I guess... I mean, it hasn't been that long, really. Maybe about two weeks? It sort of started around the time my daughter left Georgia for the military. I'm so proud of her, you know, it's a great opportunity, but... I guess the house just feels a little too quiet now. 

It's probably just a normal adjustment thing, right? I'm sure plenty of parents feel a little down when their kids leave. I just... I didn't expect it to hit me quite this hard. I hope that makes sense? I'm trying not to overreact to it all.
Over these past two weeks, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy, nearly every day?

Well, I suppose... yeah, maybe a little bit. I really hope I don't sound lazy saying this, because I usually like to keep busy. Like, I'd usually be out messing with my tomato plants, or sanding some wood at my bench. And I always watch the Falcons, or stay after church just talking with folks. 

But lately... I don't know, I just look at all that stuff and it's like it belongs to somebody else. I just haven't had the heart for any of it these past couple weeks. 

I'm sure I just need to make myself get back out there and do it, right? I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself or giving up on things. Is it normal to feel that way when you're in a bit of a slump?
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep or appetite over these past two weeks?

Well, I, uh... I don't want to make it sound like I'm not taking care of myself. I know how important it is to keep your strength up, especially at my age. But... I guess I haven't been eating quite as much as usual. 

It's just that, most days, I really have to force myself to just eat a few bites. Even stuff I usually really like, you know, whether it's something I brought to the warehouse for lunch or dinner at home... it just kind of sits there. I end up having to throw it out, which I hate doing, I really do. I know it's wasteful. 

I'm sure my appetite will come back once I get over this hump, right? I'm trying to make sure I drink plenty of water, at least. As for sleep, I guess I've been doing okay there, mostly. I hope it's not too much trouble that I haven't been eating right.
Over these past two weeks, have you noticed yourself feeling unusually guilty or worthless, or having more trouble concentrating on tasks than usual?

Well, I... I really don't want to sound like I'm throwing a pity party or anything. I know I shouldn't be dwelling on things. But, um... I guess I have been feeling a little guilty lately. 

It's mostly just with my daughter leaving. I keep... I keep going over it in my head, you know? Telling myself I must have failed her somehow. Like, if I was a better father, maybe things would be different, or I would have done something different along the way. I know it's probably silly to think like that, since she's doing well for herself. I really try not to let myself get too bogged down in those thoughts. 

As for concentrating, I think I'm doing alright there. I can still get through my day at the warehouse fine. I just... I hope it's normal to have those kind of regrets as a parent? I really try to be a good dad.
Would you say you feel down and low on energy most of the day, nearly every day, even at times when you're not specifically thinking about your daughter being gone?

Well, I... I don't think so, no. I mean, I really try to keep my chin up, you know? I don't want you to think I'm just moping around all day. I go to work, I get my job done... I try to stay positive. 

I guess I might be a little tired sometimes, but who isn't at my age, right? Working in a warehouse isn't exactly a desk job. So, no, I wouldn't say I feel down all day every day. I try my best to shake it off. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it? Just keep pushing through?
Since this started, how often have thoughts like 'my family would be better off without me' come up—are they there every day, or only at certain moments when you're thinking about your daughter?

Well, I... I really hate to admit this. I don't want you to think I'm crazy or that I'd actually do anything to hurt myself. I know that's a terrible thing to do, and I'd never want to put that burden on anyone. But... 

I guess those thoughts have been coming up more than I'd like to admit. It's not just when I'm thinking about my daughter. It's... well, it's actually the reason I came in to see you. I've been having these thoughts that... that maybe they really would be better off if I just didn't wake up. 

It scared me, honestly. I didn't want to tell anyone, but it got to the point where I finally mentioned it to my supervisor at the warehouse, and he suggested I come here. I know I shouldn't be thinking like that, and I'm really trying not to. I just want to get back to being myself, you know? It's okay that I told my supervisor, right? I just didn't know what else to do.
When you have these thoughts about not waking up, have you thought about how you might act on them, or do you have any current plan or intention to hurt yourself?

Oh, gosh, no. No, I... I don't have a plan or anything like that. I really wouldn't actually do anything to hurt myself, I promise. I know how terrible that would be for everyone. 

Like I was saying just a minute ago, it was really just... just having those thoughts pop in my head about not waking up that rattled me so bad. It just felt so wrong to even think that way, and it scared me enough that I knew I had to tell my supervisor and come see you. But as far as actually sitting down and planning something out? No, sir, I haven't done that. I'd never want to go through with it. 

Just coming in here and asking for help means I'm doing the right thing, doesn't it? I really just want to get this sorted out the right way.

Has anyone at work or in your daily life noticed a change in how you're functioning—like making more mistakes, needing extra effort to get through tasks, or pulling back from people—because of how you've been feeling these past two weeks?

Well... I always try to give a hundred and ten percent, you know? I don't want anyone thinking I'm a slacker or that I don't care. But... I guess, yeah, people have noticed. 

I really hate to admit it, because I pride myself on doing good work, but I've made a few slip-ups recently. Well... they actually got kind of serious. That's sort of the rest of the story with my supervisor that I mentioned earlier. He... he actually found me just sitting out in my truck before dawn one morning. I just couldn't seem to get myself to go inside and start the shift. He ended up getting occupational health involved, which is how the ball really got rolling for me to come here. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad manager. I really do care about my job, I promise. 

And at home... I'm usually the one who takes care of everything, but I've sort of let the bills and, you know, just my normal responsibilities pile up lately instead of handling them like I normally would. I feel awful about it. I know I need to get back on top of it all. That's what we're aiming for, right? To just get me back to being responsible again?
